stem: Lucian is a six-week-old infant with projectile non-bilious vomiting. An urgent ultrasound confirms hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. Which ultrasound measurement is an estimate used to diagnose hypertrophic pyloric stenosis?
explanation: Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis is diagnosed on ultrasound by pyloric muscle thickening, typically >3 mm. Pyloric channel length may also be increased, but not all listed measurements are standard diagnostic criteria, so 'All of the above' is incorrect.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

optionExplanations.A: Correct: pyloric muscle thickness >3 mm is a key ultrasound criterion for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect: pyloric channel length can be increased, but this range is not the standard diagnostic estimate given here.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect: pyloric diameter is not the usual diagnostic measurement used in this way.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect: not all of the listed measurements are accepted diagnostic criteria.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain
source.questionTextHtml:
You have successfully inserted an intravenous cannula and given IV fluids. You have been lucky to obtain an urgent abdominal ultrasound, which has confirmed hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. Which of the following is an estimate measurements to diagnose hypertrophic pyloric stenosis?

Pyloric muscle wall thickness > 3 mm

Pylorus diameter > 12 mm
source.stimulusText:
2

Clinical scenario 4 - Lucian

Next to be seen is Lucian, a six week old male infant presenting with projectile non-bilious vomiting after feeds for the past two weeks, now increasing in frequency. Lucian’s mother has noted a macular rash on his chest and a wrinkly appearance of his skin.

The following six questions refer to Lucian's clinical scenario.
